options.corevk.crash_graphics_api_toolti:
Graphics used after a launch that did not finish.
"Vulkan" keeps shader packs. "OpenGL" draws none. "Game default" is the game's rescue.
options.corevk.shadow_distance_tooltip:
Terrain and entities past this range cast no shadow.
Lower is faster. "Off" skips the shadow map.
Applies at once. No pack reload.
options.corevk.shadow_distance_forced: This pack already set a shadow distance. The slider cannot move.
options.corevk.shadow_map_scale_tooltip:
Share of the pack's shadow map that is actually drawn.
Lower is faster, and edges get softer or coarser. "100%" is what the pack asked for.
Reloads the pack.
options.corevk.render_scale_tooltip:
Resolution the world is drawn at, as a share of the window.
Lower is faster. AMD FSR 1.0 then fills the window. The interface stays sharp.
Applies at the next frame. No pack reload.
options.corevk.temporal_fold_tooltip:
Folds several upscaled frames into one, so a lower Render Scale keeps more detail.
Distant leaves and fences stop crawling. Things that move keep a faint trail.
Needs a Render Scale under 100%.
Applies at the next frame. No pack reload.
options.corevk.shadow_amortisation_toolt:
How many frames the shadow map is kept before it is drawn again.
Higher is faster: drawing it is the most expensive pass of the frame.
Only the GROUND ages: a block you place or break keeps its old shadow that long.
Applies at the next frame. No pack reload.
options.corevk.module_cache_ceiling_tool:
How much compiled-shader disk this engine may keep.
"512 MiB" is what it ships. Lower drops unused units sooner.
Applies at once. No pack reload.
options.corevk.compile_card_tooltip:
Shows the CoreVK mark and "Compiling shaders..." in the bottom-right corner while a pack compiles.
Off hides the corner. The F3 screen still says it.
Applies at once.
